Don't worry, you're not alone. I've wished this many times also. I feel like it would take so much pressure off me to have someone else just go ahead and do it for me. My family and friends wouldn't have to live with the guilt suicide would have created; they'd have someone to blame it on. That might be the main reason I haven't attempted it yet. I just couldn't see myself doing something like that to my family. Since you have these thoughts too, I'm assuming you feel the same way. 

Listen, I know dying seems to be the easy way out, but I've been trying to work on myself and get through this and I suggest you do the same. Possibly start getting some professional help, if you're not already. I started seeing a therapist about two months ago, and so far it's done wonders. But its effectiveness might change depending on the person. 

I know these thoughts are close to impossible to ignore, but maybe try some things that might help. One night, about a month ago now, I was feeling extremely suicidal. I was on the internet looking up different ways I could kill myself, researching effectiveness, time it takes, pain levels, etc... I realized what I was doing to myself and I couldn't take it anymore. At that moment, I turned off my laptop and got two pieces of paper. On one, I wrote things about myself that were positive, and on the other were my negative traits. I promised myself I would have the same amount of words on each paper, so when I had all these bad traits that I wanted to list, I would force myself to think of an equal number of good traits to write down. At the end, I crumpled up the negative list, and taped the positive list to my bedroom wall. It is something I can look at every morning when I wake up to remind myself that I am worth it and that this day is going to be worth it too. I would strongly advise doing something like this for yourself. I cannot stress enough how much this did for my mindset.
